460: The last paper plane carried no crossed-out sketch. It carried a drawing of you, watering your plants by the sill, with Biscuit asleep at your feet. This time, the painter drew the person who kept that little window peaceful.
464: The first time Biscuit came to eat, a little note was tucked into the ribbon on his collar: “My name is Na. Biscuit likes to sneak up to the attic. If you see him, please feed him—don’t chase him away, poor thing.”
465: The Secret at the Back Desk
466: After three cosy meals of warm milk and crunchy biscuits, Biscuit carried home his ribbon with a pressed daisy from you. In return, little Na wrote a note: she had just changed schools, and at break time she sat alone at the back desk, feeling a bit sad. You sent a small, sweet gift and a warm wish back with Biscuit.
468: The note is written in careful handwriting: “Because of your present, a girl in my class talked to me today! We played together too. I drew you a picture of us holding hands!”
469: A Rainy Night and a Glass Marble
470: One stormy night, Biscuit wandered up to the attic, soaked and shivering. Under your warm yellow lamp, wrapped in a soft dry towel, the little cat slept soundly. The next day, little Na thanked you over and over and gave you a clear glass marble. Whenever you touch it, you can almost hear the waves.
472: Once your little garden was in full bloom, little Na sent up a crayon drawing of your window, with happy news: a new girl had moved to her class and sat alone at the back desk, and this time it was Na who brought biscuits and sat beside her.
